claims.statement: Tom Allen wrote to Billy Harding of the New York News challenging Joe Coburn to fight for $2,500 a side or more, in Canada within fifty miles of Detroit, with no excursion and twenty men per party.
claims.excerpt: fight him for $2,500 a side, or as much more
places: Canada, within fifty miles of Detroit, Michigan

claims.statement: Tom Allen wrote to a friend in New York offering to fight Jem Mace a stand-up fight under the new London prize ring rules, two to four months from signing, for $2,000 to $5,000 a side, in Kansas, New Orleans or Canada.

claims.statement: Jem Mace replied from London, through a New York sporting man, that if Allen meant business he would return to America and make the match.

claims.statement: About a week before the article, Jem Mace privately wrote that he would accept and fight Allen if Allen posted a deposit at the Clipper office or Wilkes' Spirit to show he meant business.

claims.statement: If Mace would not agree, Allen offered to fight Joe Coburn at the same places, wagering $2,500 to Coburn's $1,500, or to fight Ben Hogan for $1,000 to $5,000 with as much training time as Hogan wanted.
